newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Scottish minister angry at EU salmon snub.
newsitem.headline: Scottish minister angry at EU salmon snub.

text.p: Scottish Fisheries Minister Raymond Robertson said on Thursday he was angry and disappointed at the European Union's continued refusal to protect Scotland's farmed salmon producers against cheap Norwegian imports.
"It really is a kick in the teeth to our producers and processors," Robertson said in a statement after raising the issue at a meeting of EU fisheries ministers.
Robertson added that the industry should normally have been enjoying a christmas boom but was instead having to lay off staff in order to survive.
EU Fisheries Commissioner Emma Bonino explained that there were three main reasons why she was against imposing minimum prices on imports of farmed salmon from Norway.

Firstly, salmon prices, although weaker than last year, were on an upward trend. Secondly, minimum import prices during the first half of 1996 failed to stabilise the salmon market and were extremely difficult for customs authorities to enforce.
Thirdly, the Commission was reluctant to take any action while an anti-dumping inquiry into Norwegian salmon was completed next May.
"The Commission is against safeguard measures unless it can clearly be shown that Norwegian salmon prices represent unfair competition," an official quoted Bonino as saying.
Robertson said that Bonino had accepted an invitation to go to Scotland in the New Year to explain her decision.
